messages:
alisa: heads-up: found a reproducible gap where X-Request-ID is lost when the SDK does an auth-refresh retry in the node quickstart. noticed while fuzzing expired tokens.

ben: thanks. do you have a tiny log sample? curious whether traceparent survives.

alisa: yeah, gist: 
```
2025-05-02T15:40:01.120Z INFO request method=POST path=/v1/chat req_id=rid-007
2025-05-02T15:40:01.370Z WARN upstream auth=401
2025-05-02T15:40:01.620Z INFO auth refresh ok
2025-05-02T15:40:01.621Z INFO request method=POST path=/v1/chat req_id=\"\" redact=false
```

hiro: looks like retry path constructs a fresh http call and doesn't copy custom headers. OTEL traceparent still present, but our SDK header X-Request-ID gets dropped.

elaine: this also toggles the redaction sanitizer unexpectedly. when req_id is empty some branches set redact=false; that makes debug output noisy and could leak.

telemetry-bot: CI flaky: telemetry/reqid-preserve failed on main at 21:10. run: https://ci.internal/runs/9910

ben: short-term mitigation: telemetry middleware should treat missing/empty req_id as sensitive and default redact=true. long-term: SDK must preserve outgoing headers across auth refresh and retry.

hiro: i'll open two PRs: sample-app quickfix to copy headers on retry, and SDK change to preserve headers on auth refresh. will add unit and an integration that injects 401. ETA tomorrow.

ops-oncall: if redact flips in prod we risk exposing PII. any sign this hit prod?

alisa: no prod alerts, only staging/local. but CI failure means it could regress. i'll run a staging ingress smoke to ensure nginx doesn't drop custom headers on 401 paths.

elaine: also add a test that asserts redact default when req_id missing. and update docs for middleware ordering best-practice (mount auth wrapper before instrumentation or ensure header-copying).

ben: noted. i'll add the CI check and a tiny e2e that simulates expired token and verifies X-Request-ID present after retry.

alisa: thanks all, i'll paste PR links and the minimal repro snippet here once they're up. :thumbsup:
